summary: Build the art direction from value lanes, boundaries, patterns and state shapes so meaningful graphics and controls survive palette changes, lighting and post effects.
objective: Selection, status and explanatory boundaries remain readable without hue alone, while high contrast still feels authored across unlike objects.
applies_when: A stylized 3D view contains meaningful graphics, controls, selection or status.
Lighting, bloom, fog or palette compression may erase application cues.
intent_signals: stylized scene readable without color alone
high contrast selection and error cues
accessible palette with patterns and outlines
example_prompts: Style a heart valve diagram and a product configurator with shared dark-light lanes; keep selected, obstructed and warning states distinct in grayscale.
negative_signals: Using red versus green as the only state distinction.
Measuring a beauty render and assuming every animated backdrop passes.
not_for: A blanket assertion that every decorative edge needs a 3:1 ratio.
Clinical color standards or domain-specific safety certification.

principles: Assign values by semantic layer: background, subject mass, internal boundary, annotation and active state. Hue can enrich the system but does not carry the only distinction.
Pair meaningful state color with at least one authored boundary, pattern, icon, label, thickness or shape change. Choose cues that remain visible in the actual camera and scale.
Treat lighting, fog, bloom, tone mapping and transparency as part of the contrast result. Recheck target states against every declared backdrop rather than approving isolated swatches.
implementation: In Blender, preview two unlike subjects in grayscale and under the planned key/fill. Author geometry boundaries, texture patterns or material separations for meaningful regions; keep decorative variation free where it does not convey state.

Export stable geometry/material assignments and baked patterns through glTF. Compositor outlines, view transforms and procedural marks are not assumed to transfer; record whether Three.js rebuilds them with geometry, textures, material logic or postprocessing.

In Three.js, apply state cues after the final lighting/post stack is known, expose equivalent semantic labels or controls where interaction requires them, and test adjacent colors in the rendered target state rather than raw constants.
observable_checks: Switch to grayscale and compare selected/unselected plus normal/warning: each meaningful state retains a boundary, pattern, label, icon, thickness or shape distinction.

Measure required UI/state-identification and explanatory graphic parts against adjacent colors in representative target frames; document essential-presentation or inactive exceptions instead of broadening the rule.
Sweep bright, dark and textured backdrops plus bloom/fog extrema: state outlines and explanatory boundaries do not disappear or invert unnoticed.

creative_affordances: Use split-value masses, patterned hatching, thick contour accents or luminous inset cues; accessibility constraints do not select one aesthetic.
Reserve saturated color for focus while retaining an independent boundary or symbol.
known_limits: WCAG criteria apply to web content and include scoped exceptions; this profile does not certify a whole 3D experience or establish domain-specific safety colors.
Contrast varies with the rendered adjacent pixels and state. No browser, display or assistive-technology test was run.

claims.statement: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.1 requires that color not be the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response or distinguishing a visual element.
claims.scope: Level A web-content criterion; this record proposes additional cues but does not claim conformance from a palette alone.

claims.statement: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.11 requires at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors for visual information needed to identify authored UI components and states, and for parts of graphical objects needed to understand content, subject to its inactive, user-agent and essential-presentation exceptions.
claims.scope: Level AA web-content criterion, limited to required identifying or explanatory visual information rather than all decorative 3D edges.
